description:
# Goal

Make every repeated evaluation of a product blocked on another product follow an exact recorded trigger, or prove and encode the distinct request cause that legitimately requires the retry.

## Observed defect

After fz-tfn.8 exposes ExecutableEffects recursion as ordinary ProductMemo dependency edges, the three long-lived target fixtures report 3 / 5 / 13 additional unexplained producer evaluations in every request scenario. Each new record is a recursive ExecutableEffects member with a prior ExecutableEffects(callee) wait and no ProductSettlement, ProductCacheHit, or displacement movement between the prior and repeated evaluation. This evidence identifies a generic product-wait retry symptom; it does not yet establish which driver, request, or arbitration edge is missing.

## Model and scope

Investigate the generic ProductDriver/ProductMemo wait protocol. A blocked product formula must not be retried merely because unrelated work or a drain occurred. Any required retry must be named by exact structured product identity and causal movement. Do not add an ExecutableEffects-specific gate, retry path, reverse graph, or causality exception.

## TDD and acceptance

- Reproduce the retry with the smallest generic pending-product graph, including self and mutual recursion.
- Prove whether the repeated evaluation is necessary; remove it if not, or publish the exact missing trigger if it is.
- Exact blocked dependency replacement, recursive-group publication, displacement, and cache-hit behavior remain correct.
- The 3 / 5 / 13 target-fixture unexplained deltas disappear or become exactly attributed without exclusions.
- Product values, generations, canonical cross-process traces, backend artifacts, and runtime output remain deterministic.
- Update causal baselines and performance documentation from measured evidence.
- Run focused ProductMemo/ProductDriver tests, full library, target causal/equivalence tests, fixture matrix, formatting, and clippy with warnings denied.
title: Attribute and eliminate untriggered recursive-product retries
